reasons: Correctly identified deviation: p0088 vests all IP in the Work, expressly including Improvements/Modifications that the Customer commissions and pays for under Schedule "D", with no licence back and no Customer Data ownership provision — squarely against the IP rule.

Redline is directionally right and complete against the rule: it narrows Vendor ownership to pre-existing IP, assigns the paid-for Modifications/work product to Sparkling, adds a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back for embedded Garman IP, adds a Customer Data ownership sentence (expressly covering data converted under Section 4(b)), and excludes joint ownership.

Vendor's ownership of its own platform is preserved ('as it exists independently of this Agreement'), so the edit is no broader than the rule requires; the 0.304 changed-character ratio reflects a rule-mandated reversal of ownership direction rather than gratuitous rewriting, and the added 'Except as expressly provided in this Agreement' carve-out is needed to reconcile the no-transfer sentence with the new assignment.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the playbook fallback (perpetual licence in lieu of assignment) if Garman must retain title to modifications of its own code; the only imprecision is describing the pre-existing IP as 'Software and Documentation' where the clause says 'Work', which does not mislead.
